abstract: Biomedical artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relies on heterogeneous data sources, yet differences in data structure, terminology, evidence quality, and provenance complicate their integration into reliable knowledge resources. Here, we develop an evidence-aware framework for processing and integrating heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data from FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and electronic health records in Mass General Brigham.

title: Efficient Pulse Formation to Stabilize SEI Film and Improve Performance of Commercial Lithium-ion Batteries
abstract: Pulse formation can shorten the production time of lithium-ion batteries, but the optimal current density remains unclear. This work systematically investigates the effects of five pulse formation rates (0.5 C, 0.8 C, 1.0 C, 1.15 C, and 1.25 C) on the structure and performance of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) in commercial lithium iron phosphate (LFP)/graphite cylindrical batteries. The reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced to optimize the forming process parameters globally.

title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
abstract: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.

title: Automated generation and execution of large-scale semidefinite programs for variational two-electron reduced density matrix theory
abstract: The variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) method provides a wave-function-free approach to the description of strong electron correlation whose computational cost scales polynomially with the number of correlated orbitals. Here, we present an automated pipeline for the generation and execution of semidefinite programs (SDPs) associated with the v2RDM problem. Algebraic constraints encoding ensemble $N$-representability conditions are generated via the p$^\dagger$q second-quantized algebra package, and the p$^\dagger$q-generated expressions are automatically translated into a sparse-matrix representation that can be digested by an appropriate SDP solver. We have implemented a boundary-point SDP (BPSDP) solver in the libsdp package that can execute the v2RDM SDPs on either CPU or GPU hardware. We apply the code in several contexts. First, two-particle conditions are used to describe the 76-orbital model of the iron-molybdenum cofactor (FeMoco) of nitrogenase, the simulation of which requires roughly 25 hours of compute time on a single Nvidia H100 GPU. Second, the performance of high-order (four-particle positivity) conditions is evaluated on a challenging two-dimensional H$_{10}$ cluster problem. Lastly, new classes of positivity constraints for mixed fermion-boson systems are generated and applied within the context of ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics simulations.

title: AI Mindmeld: A Latent Interconnect Protocol
abstract: LLMs can act as scientific agents using tools to consult specialists and run experiments. Yet specialist information must enter their context, generally as text, images, audio or video: a bottleneck between models with rich, high-dimensional representations. We advocate direct representation exchange: a mindmeld conveying many properties, including information an LLM would not think to request. It should be extensible to new specialists, flexible across questions and tasks, and compositional across independently connected specialists without joint training. The Latent Interconnect Protocol (LIP) learns connectors mapping specialist representations into LLM internal states. Training only connectors keeps this practical as LLMs grow and evolve. We connect three protein and three small molecule specialists to Gemma 3 (4B and 12B parameters) and Kimi K2.6 (1T total, 32B active), freezing all pretrained models. Independently trained connectors provide useful information without changing the LLM or existing connectors, supporting familiar and new question types about unseen objects. We demonstrate zero-shot transfer to cross-domain tasks without joint training. Task performance and compositionality generally improve with LLM capability, with especially strong gains in zero-shot task transfer. Limitations remain: current LLMs were not trained for specialist representations as native inputs; access does not ensure reliable interpretation, integration or use in reasoning. We call on specialist developers to provide consistent representation interfaces and, especially, on LLM developers to train models to receive, combine and reason with these inputs. These efforts could expand scientific agents' information while preserving conventional tools' flexibility. Data, pretrained connectors, and code for training, evaluation and interactive inference: https://github.com/PolymathicAI/AI-Mindmeld

title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
abstract: Donor substitution can tune the coupled ferroelectric, dielectric, electronic, and optical properties of perovskite oxides by modifying lattice distortions and electronic screening. We investigate these effects in La-doped BaTiO3 using density functional theory, density-functional perturbation theory, and the Berry-phase formalism for polarization. For a model with 12.5% La substitution at the Ba site, La incorporation induces anisotropic lattice contraction, reduces tetragonality and Ti off-centering, and weakens the energetic stabilization of the tetragonal ferroelectric phase. The accompanying reduction in polarization is associated with enhanced electronic screening and reduced anomalous Born effective charges. Phonon calculations indicate that the relaxed doped structure is dynamically stable, while hardening of a low-frequency polar mode is consistent with weakened ferroelectricity. The high-frequency dielectric response increases moderately, whereas the static dielectric response decreases as the lattice contribution is suppressed. Electronic-structure calculations show a Fermi-level shift toward the conduction band without mid-gap defect states. The optical spectra exhibit an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein-Moss-type mechanism, enhanced near-edge transparency, and reduced birefringence. Together, these results suggest a microscopic connection between donor-induced screening, polar-mode hardening, reduced dynamical charges, polarization suppression, and decreased optical anisotropy. The conclusions apply to the investigated 12.5% composition; calculations at additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.

title: GANet: A Lightweight Group Attention Network for Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Systems
abstract: Global warming and climate change are major catalysts for plant diseases, significantly affecting food production worldwide. Addressing this issue requires continuous monitoring and early detection of plant diseases. While recent advancements in deep learning offer potential solutions, most models demand high processing power and struggle to perform efficiently on low-end electronic hardware. Furthermore, many existing works focus on specific crop diseases, limiting their broader applicability. This paper presents a lightweight Group Equivariance Attention Network (GANet) designed for the prediction and monitoring of 38 types of plant diseases. GANet introduces a novel Group Attention block and Group-Wise Feature Fusion block, making it both sparse and efficient. With only 0.001M parameters, the model achieves an impressive 99.99% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset. Additionally, GANet is optimized for deployment on edge devices such as the Raspberry Pi 4b and Jetson Nano, where it reaches 5 FPS and 11 FPS, respectively, demonstrating its potential for real-time plant disease monitoring on low-power devices.

title: Data-efficient molecular and nanoparticle design via fine-tuned large language models
abstract: Designing molecules with prescribed properties is central to pharmaceutical and materials innovation, but vast chemical design spaces make development lengthy and costly. Generative artificial intelligence can accelerate molecular discovery, but its deployment in many real-world domains remains limited by the need for large task-specific training datasets. To enable generative design when property-labeled data are scarce, we present a data-efficient foundation-model adaptation strategy combining complementary positive and negative property prompts with parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

title: Cationic surfactant-modified cotton and cotton/polyester textile-derived biochar for hexavalent chromium removal via ion-exchange
abstract: Biochar derived from textile waste presents an opportunity in the circular economy for contaminant remediation from industrial wastewater. In this study, biochars derived from cotton and cotton-polyester blended textiles were assessed for the removal of the toxic and pervasive aqueous contaminant, hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)). Unmodified textile-derived biochars exhibited some adsorption capacity for Cr(VI) under environmentally relevant pH conditions, but removal improved substantially once modified with the cationic surfactant cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB).

title: Spatially Separated NO Capture and Hydrogenation for NH 3 Synthesis from O 2 -Containing Streams
abstract: The selective conversion of nitric oxide (NO) in combustion flue gases to ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising strategy for sustainable nitrogen management. However, this conversion remains challenging in O 2 -containing exhaust gases because coexisting O 2 strongly inhibits catalytic hydrogenation. Here, we developed a tandem NO capture and hydrogenation system for NH 3 production from O 2 -containing streams.

title: Pyrrolidinium-Assisted Proton and Cation Exchange Enables Near-Quantitative Rare Earth Extraction from Synthetic NdFeB Leachate
abstract: Diglycolamide (DGA) extractants offer strong affinity for rare-earth elements (REEs), tunable coordination, and phosphorus-free chemistry. Incomplete use of their molar capacity limits extractant utilization efficiency (EUE), while low distribution ratios (D) require larger organic-phase volumes. Ionic liquids (ILs) can stabilize DGA–REE complexes and modify extraction pathways, with proton exchange reported in some imidazolium ILs and IL-mediated cation or anion exchange in others.

title: Chemical Representation Dependence of Quinone Reduction Energetics: Site-Specific Limits of Methylthio Surrogates for Cysteine-Derived Conjugates
abstract: Methylthio substituents are compact models for larger sulfur-linked quinone conjugates, yet their fidelity for calculated one-electron reduction-energy shifts is uncertain. We audited a historical survey of 38 methylthio attachment sites in 26 quinones; four source-energy outputs remain unreconciled, leaving 34 archive-corroborated site shifts across 25 parents. In a historical matched comparison of ten SMe and N-acetylcysteine methyl ester-derived (AcCysOMe) conjugate models, the original median absolute mismatch was 0.175900 eV.

title: Fabrication and Microstructural Analysis of ZnO and In2O3 MOS Thin Film Sensors with Embedded Microheaters for Methane Sensing
abstract: Methane detection is essential for both environmental monitoring and industrial safety due to its greenhouse impact and explosive potential. Conventional sensing approaches, such as electrochemical, infrared, and catalytic bead sensors, are limited by stability and sensitivity constraints. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors, particularly those based on ZnO and In2O3, provide an attractive alternative owing to their stability, high sensitivity, compactness, and fabrication compatibility.

title: What a low-bias filter leaves out: measured performance on the excluded negatives of a drug–target interaction benchmark
abstract: Eligibility rules define which interactions contribute to a benchmark score. The low-bias BindingDB benchmark retains a drug only when it has both positive and negative labels, excluding measured inactive pairs involving drugs without a measured active. We reconstructed this rule in a declared BindingDB population and evaluated retained and excluded negatives against the same positive reference. After cleaning and an additional connectivity-overlap restriction, the excluded region contained 78.4% of the measured negative pairs.

title: Toward Interpretable Graph-Based Machine Learning for Combustion Kinetic Model Generation
abstract: This work presents an atom-conserving and interpretable graph neural network (GNN) for combustion kinetic model generation, where atoms are represented as nodes, covalent bonds are represented as edges, and reactions are represented as bond-rearrangement operations. Its artificial-intelligence (AI) contribution is a reaction generator that extends a standard Graph Isomorphism Network with Edges (GINE) architecture through reaction-context embeddings, reaction branching & third-body reaction inputs, Arrhenius-rate-parameter prediction, pairwise decoding, and stochastic inference over evolving…

title: Accelerating Catalyst Discovery with Artificial Intelligence Using Molecular Dual-Atom Site Catalysts as a Case Study
abstract: We test whether researchers can delegate the writing of a complete catalyst study to a large language model while retaining scientific judgment. Our case study concerns molecular dual-atom site catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction, where stabilizing an adsorbed intermediate can make its subsequent reduction less favorable. Using density functional theory calculations on 88 catalysts, we explain this balance through adsorption free energies and the overpotential volcano.
authors: Bruno Ina cio da Silva Roux Leite

title: Generative discovery, symmetry-aware membership screening, and device-level evaluation of six-member-ring MoS2 polytypes
abstract: Six-membered-ring (SMR) inorganic materials were recently unified into a class, but the class-level perspective lacks two enabling tools: an operational test of “SMR-ness” and a path from newly generated crystals to device-level figures of merit. Here we couple conditional generative modelling (MatterGen; Mo–S, Ti–S, W–Se; 512 cells per system) to a novelty/stability funnel, a symmetry-aware membership checker that casts the SMR definition as three calibrated criteria (6/6 positives, 6/6 trap negatives), full DFT relaxation with composition-anchored hull analysis, and a contract-based device…

title: Mechanical versus thermal amorphization of ZIF-4: from local rearrangements to network disorder
abstract: There is mounting evidence that different amorphization routes can produce metalorganic framework (MOF) glasses with distinct structures and properties, yet the microscopic origins of these differences remain difficult to establish experimentally. Focusing on the two main synthesis methods, which are melt-quenching and ball-milling, we use molecular dynamics simulations with a machine-learning interatomic potential to compare different glasses obtained from ZIF-4.

title: Dynamic Anionic Speciation and Proton Transfer in Choline/Geranic Acid Mixtures Revealed by Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
abstract: In carboxylate/carboxylic acid-containing ionic liquid systems, oligomeric complex anions have been shown to substantially alter transport properties; yet whether such persistent pairing survives in the presence of water remains an open question. The 1:2 choline/geranic acid mixture (CAGE12) provides an ideal case study: a promising therapeutic solvent unavoidably hydrated in biomedical use.

title: Two-photon-enabled near-infrared proximity labeling maps protein neighborhoods in vivo
abstract: Native molecular neighborhoods govern biological processes and disease, yet existing approaches trade off penetration, precision, and native compatibility. Photocatalytic proximity labeling (PL) offers nanoscale, genetics-free precision but is limited by visible-light activation in optically opaque tissue. Here, we report 2PMap, a two-photon near-infrared PL platform driven by a sensitizer with a twophoton absorption cross-section nearly two orders of magnitude above conventional photocatalysts, enabling 850 nm continuous-wave excitation without pulsed lasers.

title: Morgan Fingerprint Classification Prioritizes Autophagy Modulators While Transcriptome Regression Fails to Distinguish Opposing Modulators
abstract: Autophagy is a conserved lysosomal degradation and recycling pathway with established roles in aging, neurodegeneration, cancer, and metabolic disease. Computational prioritization of autophagy modulators is difficult: autophagy modulators have a variety of mechanisms and the analysis of perturbational transcriptomes could confound pathway-specific effects with generic stress responses.

title: Functional-Group Effects in Biopolymer Binders for Sodium-Ion Battery Electrodes: Interfaces, Rheology, and Electrochemical Performance
abstract: Binders, though typically only a few weight percent of a battery electrode, play an outsized role in determining cell performance and sustainability. Water-soluble green binders have emerged as eco-friendly alternatives that enable aqueous slurry processing and easier recyclability. In this work, we leverage biopolymer-based binders (CMC/SBR, Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) in sodium-ion battery electrodes (Prussian white cathodes and hard carbon anodes) to demonstrate a new paradigm of sustainable electrode design.

title: Atom-precise nanocluster architectures programmed by biomolecular assembly
abstract: Ligand-protected metal nanoclusters hold promise as atomically precise building blocks for nanoscale materials. However, it remains challenging to achieve ligand chemistries that control higher-order organization while still retaining the nanocluster’s atom-precise properties. Here, we present two biomolecular approaches for higher-order organization of silver nanoclusters stabilized by DNA (DNA-Ag N ). First, using strategies from DNA nanotechnology, we develop complementary DNA-Ag N that oligomerize upon toehold-mediated strand displacement reactions.

title: Improving Molecular Dynamics of Aqueous Electrolytes through Data-Driven Sensitivity-Guided GFN2-xTB Reparameterization
abstract: Semiempirical tight-binding methods such as GFN2-xTB enable efficient molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, but their performance is strongly system dependent. The default GFN2-xTB parameterization overestimates equilibrium densities of liquid water and aqueous NaCl, and it underestimates the bond length for Na+–water pairs in the radial distribution function. To correct these deficiencies, we develop a sensitivity-guided stepwise approach to reparameterize GFN2-xTB against cluster-based and periodic revPBE0-D3 data.

title: Chiral Organic Single Crystals as a Platform for Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
abstract: The chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect has attracted increasing attention for its unique ability to generate spin-polarized currents without magnetic components, with promising applications in spintronics, optoelectronics, and electrocatalysis. Although a wide range of chiral materials have been demonstrated to exhibit the CISS effect, most reported systems are based on amorphous films, self-assembled monolayers, or supramolecular assemblies, where structural disorder and aggregative traps compromise reliable evaluation of the CISS effect and obscure the structure-property…

title: Picking a Pucker: Excited-State Charge Redistribution Navigates the BN-Reshaped Conical-Intersection Landscape in Azaborine Photochemistry
abstract: Photoexcited benzene yields multiple isomers, whereas its BN isostere 1,2-azaborine selectively forms BN-Dewar benzene (BN-DB), despite both decaying through ringpuckered S1/S0 conical intersections (CIs). This selectivity is puzzling given that BNinduced asymmetry in 1,2-azaborine creates six distinct puckering sites and potentially multiple CIs, yet only a single photoproduct is observed.

title: An open-source electrosynthesis platform for reaction screening enables a nickel-catalyzed electroreductive aryl cyanation
abstract: The application of electrochemistry to synthetic organic chemistry has resulted in the development of more efficient and sustainable synthesis methodologies. However, the costs and technical burdens of electrochemical instrumentation impose barriers towards the wider adoption of electrochemistry. Herein, we report a modular, open-source platform for electrosynthesis screening built around a low-cost miniaturized potentiostat. The platform supports electrosynthesis and electroanalytic methods, and its open design readily allows for customization.

title: Synthesis of Leaching-Proof Single-Site Catalysts Based on Metallolinker MOFs
abstract: The creation of single-site catalysts, for which all active sites have the same structure, is a key goal in contemporary heterogeneous catalysis. Many MOF linkers present well-defined binding sites for transition metals and may thus provide access to single-site catalysts. Depending on how the metal is introduced into the linker-based binding site, however, additional undesired species such as pore-confined nanoparticles or node-bound metal centers may be formed that can be difficult to locate.

title: Resolving the Methanol-Promoting Alloy–Oxide Ensemble in Pd–Zn/C Catalysts for CO2 Hydrogenation
abstract: Pd–Zn bimetallic catalysts are a promising alternative to traditional Cu-based systems for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. Yet a complete understanding of their structure-activity relationships has been hindered by methodological limitations, such as high-temperature synthesis and the use of bulk characterization techniques. Here, we use an inert graphitic carbon support to prepare a Pd–Zn/C catalyst library with systematically varied Zn:Pd ratio and pre-treatment temperature.

title: Photocatalyst-Free Visible-Light-Induced Trifluoroalkylation of Electron-Deficient Heteroaromatics via a Three-Component Minisci-Type Reaction.
abstract: The combination of electron-poor heterocycles and trifluoromethyl motifs is widely found in pharmaceuticals, making the development of methods for the simultaneous introduction of these two features highly desirable. Herein, we report a fast, acid-free, metal-free, photocatalyst-free, and operationally simple multicomponent approach for the trifluoroalkylation of electron-poor heterocycles under open-air conditions.

title: Conditional latent distillation enables controllable molecular generation in data-limited soft materials
abstract: De novo molecular generation is particularly difficult when materials-specific datasets are too small to support reliable training of a new generative backbone. We develop a framework for controllable molecular generation based on conditional latent distillation and chemistryconstrained construction. A variational autoencoder (VAE) pretrained on more than 20,000 polymer molecules supplies a starting molecular representation, reducing reliance on training a new generator from approximately 1,600 surfactant or 200 anion-exchange-membrane (AEM) records.

title: Comparable Trifluoroacetic Acid Deposition in Guyana and Canada: Evidence of Atmospheric Formation and Remobilization
A Dioxasilepane-Functionalized Styrenic Monomer as a Platform for Novel Silicon-Containing Polystyrenes
abstract: A dioxasilepane-derived styrenic monomer, 2,4,4,7,7-pentamethyl-2-(4-vinylphenyl)-1,3,2-dioxasilepane (St-Si(pan)Me), is introduced as the first polymerizable representative of the recently developed Si(pan) platform, a seven-membered cyclic dialkoxysilane motif combining high stability with controllable silicon reactivity. The monomer combines the exceptional kinetic stability of the seven-membered cyclic dialkoxysilane with a polymerizable styrenic functionality, enabling direct incorporation of the Si(pan) motif into polystyrene-based polymers and materials.

title: Discovery of Nanomolar CDK2 Inhibitors Using Boltz-2
abstract: The computational design of small-molecule ligands for pharmaceutical targets has historically been hindered by a strict trade-off between screening throughput and predictive accuracy. While next-generation cofolding affinity models like Boltz-2 hold immense promise for bridging this gap, their utility in prospective medicinal chemistry campaigns remains largely unexplored. To date, virtual screens leveraging these models have been overwhelmingly restricted to standard commercial catalogs, leaving their capacity to navigate novel, synthetically tailored chemical spaces unevaluated.

title: A Novel Reactive Incipient Wetness Impregnation Assisted by H 2 O 2 for Vanadium Catalysts: the Case of V/Silicalite-1 zeolites in Oxidative Propane Dehydrogenation
abstract: Metal deposition in zeolites is often interpreted using concepts developed for relatively open support surfaces, overlooking the consequences of precursor transport and deposition within confined microporous environments. Here, we introduce an H 2 O 2 -mediated reactive impregnation strategy for supported vanadium catalysts reactive vanadium impregnation mediated by H 2 O 2 and that avoids organics complexing agents (carbon-free) exploiting vanadium-peroxo chemistry to dissolve in situ the precursor into smaller complexed soluble species and modify its interaction with Silicalite-1.

title: One-Pot Synthesis of Oxazolines from Carboxylic Acids and Amino Alcohols using Phosphorus(V) Catalysis
abstract: Oxazolines are important heterocycles for a range of industrial applications, and yet their synthesis from simple carboxylic acid and amino alcohol substrates requires multiple steps and stoichiometric reagents. Here, we demonstrate the one-pot direct synthesis using a bifunctional boronic acid/phosphorus(V) catalyst that is shown to catalyze both the amidation and cyclodehydration steps.

title: Ion Pairing and Electrochemical Behavior of Al(OTf)3 in Propylene Carbonate Bilal Overton
abstract: The development of practical aluminum-ion batteries requires electrolytes capable of stabilizing multivalent aluminum species while maintaining sufficient ionic conductivity and electrochemical activity. Here, we investigate aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTf)3) dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC) as a potential halide-free aluminum electrolyte using a combined computational and experimental approach.

title: Spontaneous Emergence of Homochiral Halogen-bonded Helices from Achiral Components
abstract: Biological systems selectively use chiral molecules, such as L-amino acids and D-sugars, to construct single-handed helical structures including proteins, collagen, and DNA. Reproducing such handedness selection using synthetic systems remains a major challenge because achiral molecules generally form racemic helices. Here, we show that supramolecular halogen-bonded complexes assembled entirely from achiral molecular components spontaneously form either left- or right-handed helices.

title: An Interpretable and Transferable Physics-Aware Machine-Learning Framework for Stability Prediction of Dual-Atom Alloys
abstract: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations.

title: From Data-Driven Personalization to Culturally Adaptive Merchandising: A Systematic Review and the CAMI-DM Framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), behavioral analytics, recommender systems, and digital retail technologies are increasingly used to personalize consumer experiences. Yet personalization based primarily on observed behavior may remain insensitive to cultural meaning, local practices, language, symbolic preferences, and context. This study revisits the literature on data-driven intelligent multicultural merchandising and develops an integrative research framework rather than a descriptive inventory of technologies. A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using Scopus.

title: Sugar-Based 1-Dimensional Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates with Hydration-Tunable Chiroptical Emission
abstract: Chiral topology in semiconductors introduces a structural degree of freedom for tuning the chiroptical, excitonic, and spintronic behavior. In metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas) semiconductors, how ligand stereochemistry and supramolecular organization influence chiral topology, and thus optical and excitonic responses, remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate intrinsic circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in sugar-based 1-dimensional MOChas, with structures solved via small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PRISM, a Bidirectional NMR Foundation Model: From Peak List to Structure and Back
abstract: Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural-product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra-to-structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak-Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder-decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1H and 13C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry-aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR-structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo-aware (72.5% stereo-unaware) top-1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine-tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top-1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision-support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni-muenster.de/.

title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
abstract: New active ingredients for drugs to treat infections, cancer or other serious diseases are often based on substances originally discovered in microorganisms, plants or other living organisms. Producing or improving such active ingredients in a targeted manner using microorganisms is often challenging because the underlying biological processes are extremely complex.

title: Sterically Shielded Cations Decouple Ion-Exchange Capacity from Water Uptake in Anion Exchange Membranes
abstract: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for electrochemical devices must combine high ion-exchange capacity (IEC) with controlled hydration and dimensional stability. Water uptake is commonly rationalized in terms of IEC and intrinsic cation hydrophilicity, but this picture fails when the cationic site is locally shielded by the polymer architecture. Using the poly(bis-imidazolium) ionene Aemion+® as a model backbone-embedded AEM, we find that it absorbs only ~40% of the water taken up by pendant-cation analogues at matched IEC, reversing the trend expected from solution thermodynamics, which…

title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
abstract: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

title: Interhalogen of Iodine Chloride Accelerates Charge Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
abstract: Li–O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mirror-image molecules are difficult to separate from their counterparts, but a new catalytic method might be the answer
abstract: Just like gloves, molecules can have left- and right-handed—or mirror-image—forms. Because the left- and right-handed molecules are still very similar, scientists have had trouble separating them from each other. But a team of researchers in Japan might have found a solution. In their new study, published in Science Advances, the team successfully separated an equal mixture of mirror-image molecules created by replacing hydrogen with deuterium in one form.

title: RecA structure kinetics determine SOS dynamics and predict spontaneous cell death
abstract: Even under optimal growth conditions, bacterial cells experience endogenous stresses that threaten cellular function. Individual cells sporadically activate stress responses to restore homeostasis, but some cells ultimately die. The SOS response to DNA damage is particularly heterogeneous, but the origin of its spontaneous activation and its relationship to cell fate remain unclear. Here, we imaged fluorescently labelled RecA in single Escherichia coli cells under steady-state unperturbed growth using microfluidics. We find that RecA* structures assemble frequently near replication forks and precede SOS response pulses. RecA* structure lifetime quantitatively encodes the magnitude of SOS induction: longer-lived structures promote greater LexA degradation and larger SOS pulses. Thus, cell-to-cell variability in spontaneous SOS activation reflects differences in the repair kinetics of endogenous DNA damage events. By tracking cell lineages over time, we further show that RecA* structures are strong and early predictors of cell fate. Elevated RecA* structure presence emerges up to six generations before spontaneous cell death in over 75% of cases, before other physiological disturbances become detectable. Together, our results establish spontaneous SOS activation as a quantitative readout of endogenous DNA damage processing and identify failure to resolve such damage as a major route to spontaneous bacterial cell death.

title: From Perception Errors to Unsafe Actions: A Survey of Behavioral Safety in MLLM Agents
abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents connect perceptual inputs to tools and external actions, making safety a property of trajectories and retained state. This curated survey uses a constrained partially observable Markov decision process to organize six risk families: grounding failure, observation manipulation, miscalibrated authority, inference-time hijacking, unsafe commitment, and reusable-state corruption. We compare safeguards by mechanism, access requirements, and evidence scope, separating direct multimodal execution from transferred model-level and text-agent findings.

title: Differentiated Determinant Graphs Enable Large-Scale Multideterminant Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo
abstract: Multideterminant trial wave functions can reduce phaseless bias in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC), but the repeated evaluation of their overlap, force bias, and local energy restricts systematic trial improvement. In this work, we organize particle--hole excitation determinants as a shared arithmetic directed acyclic graph of canonical minors. A coefficient-weighted reverse pass and batched directional passes evaluate the complete estimator without determinant-resolved cofactor tensors while preserving the sparse $α$--$β$ coefficient coupling exactly. Controlled complex-valued tests verify the complete kernel to machine precision and show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over direct determinant summation. In molecular calculations, the observed cost remains sublinear through million-configuration selected-CI trials and the same estimator remains usable at one hundred million configurations, where the eventual exact coefficient-contraction boundary becomes visible. For Cr$_2$, an orbital-optimized CAS(12e,42o) trial in a double-$ζ$ basis yields a potential-energy curve (PEC) and spectroscopic constants in close agreement with experiment. Differentiated determinant graphs therefore convert very large correlated trials from a formal accuracy hierarchy into a practical route for systematic AFQMC studies of strongly correlated molecules.

title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
abstract: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material. We find nearly-perfect insensitivity to defects only for wavevectors with single transport modes within specific Fermi level ranges in CoSi(001) and PtAl(001). Importantly, we also find high insensitivity for certain non-isolated modes in NbAs that emerge specifically due to spin-orbit coupling; these modes could not be identified previously as they were buried in the total transmission. These non-isolated modes have been buried in previous studies of total transmission, and can now be directly compared to other materials due to our standardization of defect-creation. This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
abstract: Over the past decade, substantial efforts have been devoted to developing machine learning (ML) methods for extracting materials data and, where possible, materials knowledge directly from the scientific literature. This review traces the evolution of these methods from heuristic, rule-based pipelines through natural language processing (NLP) models and transformer-based encoders to, lastly, large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems capable of extracting materials information across multiple modalities, including text, tables, and figures. Beside construction of large, queryable materials databases and knowledge graphs that support downstream materials discovery, we discuss how these advances have enabled new capabilities, such as, generic question answering across materials science, AI co-scientists and chatbots for research assistance, and closed-loop optimization and discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories. We critically assess the datasets generated using these approaches, their extraction accuracy and computational costs, and the respective strengths and limitations of different methodologies, and even provide practical guidelines for developing more reliable and scalable materials data extraction pipelines. Finally, we identify key open challenges, including the extraction of full materials structure-property-processing-performance tetrahedron at the sample level, the scarcity of reliable benchmark datasets for systematic evaluation, and the resolution of non-standard materials terminology across different document modalities.

title: SIFT-MS Enables Product-Specific Insight into Electrochemical Pulsed CO2 Reduction in Membrane Electrode Assemblies
abstract: Pulsed electrolysis is a promising operating strategy for electrochemical CO2 reduction, but understanding how products form, accumulate, and are released during dynamic operation remains challenging, particularly in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Conventional product analysis methods provide limited time resolution, making them poorly suited for resolving product-specific changes during pulses that are on the timescale of seconds.

title: afMLevel: Deep learning U-Net Models for Levelling Atomic Force Microscopy Images and Movies
abstract: AFM experiments can now produce hundreds of frames per session and this rises to thousands in the case of video-rate high-speed AFM, but every image must still be levelled to remove tilt, bowing and line noise before it can be measured. Current automatic routines rely on user-chosen masks and parameters that work for some sample types but fail on others, so levelling often remains a manual, subjective bottleneck. Here, we present two U-Net models developed using machine learning for levelling AFM images without altering the sample topography. MLMask segments features so that they are excluded from conventional plane and line background fits, and MLBackground predicts the noise and artifact background directly, which is then subtracted. Both were trained on 2,001 experimental images from multiple instruments and sample types, using manually levelled images as ground truth. On 164 unseen images, MLMask routines brought 70-80% of images below a mean squared error of 0.1 relative to manual levelling, compared with 60-70% for the best multi-plane method, with a lower mean error (0.1-0.15 vs 0.15-0.3), and both models significantly outperformed fourteen classical routines (p < 0.01). Applied frame by frame, the models process 512x512 pixel HS-AFM movies at 4.7 frames.s-1. We provide afMLevel as an openly-available package for the use of other researchers. By removing the need to choose levelling parameters image by image, this package together with its models and paired training data, provides a foundation for automated AFM analysis pipelines.

title: Choosing Spatial Resolution in the Residence-Time Approach to Local Diffusivity
abstract: Estimating position-dependent diffusivity with the residence-time approach (RTA) requires choosing an interval width that resolves spatial variation while probing time scales compatible with a local diffusion model. We develop a selection criterion that combines bulk diffusivity convergence with local model agreement measured by the Kullback-Leibler divergence between observed and predicted first-exit-time distributions, and assess global model agreement through independent propagator analysis against unbiased molecular dynamics. Applications to water in a fluid phospholipid bilayer and three permeants in a model skin lipid barrier show that local agreement alone does not ensure global fidelity: in the skin barrier, narrow intervals minimize exit-time mismatch but predict excessive spreading, whereas requiring bulk convergence selects wider intervals with better longer-time predictions. In propagator tests, RTA profiles at the selected interval widths outperform velocity-autocorrelation-based profiles and generally improve agreement relative to position-autocorrelation-based profiles in the skin barrier, while phospholipid-bilayer rankings depend on lag time and discrepancy metric; both autocorrelation methods use harmonically restrained simulations.

title: Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

title: Fast2Peak: High-Fidelity Restoration Algorithm by Single-Pixel Masking towards Real-Time Spectral Measurements
abstract: Improving the temporal and spatial resolution of spectroscopy inevitably reduces the photons available to each measurement, pushing rapid measurements into photon-starved conditions where weak spectral features are obscured by stochastic background noise. Here, we present Fast2Peak (F2P), a self-supervised Transformer framework that transforms the spectral restoration task into a context-prediction problem. Given that physically constrained spectral signals exhibit strong local continuity, whereas the stochastic noise fluctuates randomly and does not possess the continuity across neighboring spectral pixels, single-pixel masking enables F2P to restore the predictable signal structure while suppressing unpredictable fluctuations even without clean reference spectra. Unlike conventional offline spectral restoration, F2P achieves high-fidelity restoration within milliseconds, enabling real-time "acquire-and-process" operation. We demonstrate this capability in time-resolved electrochemical SERS and hyperspectral Raman imaging, where spectral restoration is performed during data acquisition. In addition, F2P has demonstrated its robust generalization across different instruments and spectral modalities, including Raman, NMR, XRD and FTIR.

title: Hierarchical Response Theory of Electronegativity from Atomic Mean Inner Potential
abstract: Electronegativity, introduced by Pauling nearly a century ago, remains chemistry's most widely used yet conceptually ambiguous quantity: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP), a quantum-mechanical observable accessible through first-principles calculation and, ultimately, electron holography. Expanding the AMIP with respect to fractional electron removal defines a hierarchy of physically distinct coefficients: the static electronegativity $χ_0$, the Electrostatic Rigidity $\mathcal{R}$---whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation---and the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus $\mathcal{A}$. A logarithmic-derivative decomposition links these coefficients to two competing microscopic channels, electronic screening loss and geometric volume collapse, whose balance governs the response of all 102 elements. This competition produces a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series (closed-shell stiffening and principal quantum softening), and two anomalies: a pronounced exchange-driven effect at half-filled d$^{5}$ configurations and a near-perfect cancellation in Ce. It also resolves the long-standing Cs--Fr controversy, identifying Fr as a critical element whose near-boundary response is amplified fivefold by relativistic contraction of the 7s orbital. The framework reproduces the classical Allen, Pauling, and Mulliken scales as well as Lewis acidity trends, and makes three falsifiable experimental predictions. It transforms electronegativity from a lookup-table number into a predictive, hierarchically structured quantum descriptor.

title: Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (MQE): A Selective State Space Model for Scalable Ground State Simulations in Quantum Chemistry
abstract: Predicting molecular electronic structure using Quantum Computing approaches is a challenge in Computational Chemistry. Traditional Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) are typically hindered by optimization challenges. The alternative Generative Quantum Eigensolver (GQE) mitigates this by reformulating ground-state search as discrete sequence generation, but its Transformer backbone suffers from quadratic computational complexity, bottlenecking scalability for larger molecules. To address this, we introduce the Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (Mamba-QE), which replaces the Transformer with a Selective State Space Model (SSM) to process operator sequences with linear $\mathcal{O}(L)$ complexity. Additionally, we integrate a distance-conditioned mechanism enabling the direct prediction of complete potential energy surfaces (PES). Evaluated on the $H_2$ molecule, Mamba-QE reproduces Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) reference energies well within chemical accuracy, achieving an energy error below $3\times10^{-6}$ Ha across 16 geometries with zero variational violations. Mamba-QE maintains high expressive power while establishing a robust, scalable foundation for quantum simulations of complex molecular systems.

title: Consistent Modeling of SEI Growth via Electron Diffusion Validated Across Diverse Cell Specifications and Operating Conditions in LFP/Graphite Cells
abstract: Understanding and predicting degradation in lithium-ion batteries is critical for their widespread deployment. The continuous growth of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) remains a dominant aging pathway, yet accurately modeling its kinetics across diverse cell specifications and operating conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we present and validate a physically grounded SEI growth model mediated by the electron diffusion mechanism. This framework intrinsically captures the state of charge (SOC) dependence of degradation through the impact of the anode potential on the electron concentration, which governs the rate of SEI growth. The presented model explicitly accounts for variations in electrolyte salt, anode material, temperature, and cycling rate. Validation against experimental aging data for LFP/graphite cells demonstrates high predictive accuracy across a broad range of cell specifications and cycling conditions, including confined SOC windows, electrolyte salts (LiFSI, LiPF6), artificial graphites (AGC, AGD), temperatures (40-70°C), and C-rates (C/20-1C). Remarkably, a single, consistent set of parameters is applied to simulate the capacity fade for all experiments without recalibration. While quantitative overestimations occur during high-SOC storage periods, the framework consistently captures the observed degradation trends. Our findings underscore that lower SOC operation mitigates degradation, establishing a physics-based model for predicting long-term lithium-ion battery aging.

title: From detection to prediction: AI-integrated molecular and biosensing approaches for psychrotrophic and thermophilic spoilage bacteria in dairy systems
abstract: Psychrotrophic Gram-negative bacteria and thermophilic or thermoduric spore-forming bacteria are major causes of quality deterioration and shelf-life loss in milk and dairy products. Their impact is mediated primarily by heat-stable peptidases and lipases, heat-resistant spores and biofilms that persist in processing environments; with the notable exception of toxigenic members of the Bacillus cereus group, most of these organisms are spoilage rather than safety hazards. Culture-based methods remain the reference standard but are slow and provide single time-point information.

title: Support Protection Mechanism Enables Efficient and Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
abstract: Designing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a critical challenge for the development of alkaline anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here, we uncover a unique support protection mechanism in which lattice-confined ruthenium (Ru) single atoms offer robust protection for the spinel Co3O4 support, realizing outstanding stability in AEMWEs.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Boosting Ionomer Oxygen Transport via Pore Confinement in Carbon Supports for Low-Pt Fuel Cells
abstract: Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Perisynaptic matrix gene variants underlie DystoniaGeneNet endophenotypes in isolated focal dystonia
abstract: Isolated focal dystonia is a rare movement disorder characterized by abnormalities in brain structure and function. The genes underlying isolated focal dystonia are not fully elucidated, and genetic studies are constrained by incomplete penetrance and small family sizes. Neuroimaging endophenotypes shared by patients and unaffected relatives can reveal genetic liability independently of clinical manifestation and offer a strategy for advancing gene discovery. We developed DystoniaGeneNet, a 3D convolutional neural network that predicts familial status from T1-weighted brain MRIs. We then used its predictions to guide genetic analyses in isolated focal dystonia. DystoniaGeneNet was trained on 40 patients with familial laryngeal dystonia and 40 healthy controls, then applied to independent cohorts of 21 patients with familial isolated focal dystonia, 364 patients with sporadic dystonia, and 98 unaffected relatives. Model predictions were incorporated into variant prioritization and segregation analysis in 214 individuals with whole-exome sequencing data, and results were replicated in another 738 independent exomes, in genetic data from a hospital-based biobank (892 dystonia cases, 2,475 controls), and in the All of Us Research Program genetic data (1,343 dystonia cases, 6,840 controls). DystoniaGeneNet discriminated familial dystonia from healthy controls in the training set and correctly classified 85.7% of independent familial cases, using a biomarker centred on the corpus callosum and inferior temporal gyrus. Across the discovery and replication cohorts, we identified rare, likely pathogenic genetic variants in RAP1GAP and TNN segregating with disease in families. Additional variants were found in singletons with isolated focal dystonia. In patients with clinically sporadic dystonia but predicted to have familial features, we observed multiple rare variants in ITSN2 , including three high-confidence loss-of-function variants, and an enrichment of damaging missense variants in its Dbl homology domain. To determine the functional impact of discovered genetic variants, we assessed gene expression and splicing via qPCR and RNA sequencing ( n = 74), revealing reduced RAP1GAP and ITSN2 expression in variant carriers. At the pathway level, rare nonsynonymous variants in brain-expressed matrisome genes were associated with dystonia ( P = 0.012). Our strategy utilizing a deep learning-derived neuroimaging endophenotype to empower gene discovery uncovered RAP1GAP, TNN , and ITSN2 as novel genes associated with isolated focal dystonia. These genes converge on perisynaptic extracellular matrix-synapse signalling, implicating a mechanism linked to synaptic plasticity deficits, and identifying a molecular substrate for network-level brain abnormalities that characterize this disorder. Further, we exemplify a generalizable framework for leveraging endophenotypes in rare neurogenetic diseases with incomplete penetrance.

title: Photoinduced Enantioselective α-Alkylation of Active Methines with Nonactivated Alkenes Using a Chiral Ytterbium Lewis Acid
abstract: Catalytic enantioselective alkylation is a fundamental strategy for constructing molecular frameworks bearing chiral carbon centers. Herein, we report a photoinduced highly enantioselective catalytic α-alkylation of active methine compounds with nonactivated alkenes to construct chiral quaternary stereocenters. Cooperative catalysis using an organophotocatalyst and a chiral ytterbium Lewis acid bearing an Indapybox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation of open-chain 2-substituted β-ketoesters, affording the desired products in high yields with high enantioselectivities (up to 96% yield…

title: Zero-group-velocity modes in textured steel plates: experiments and elastic modeling
abstract: Zero-group-velocity (ZGV) resonances are investigated as a non-contact ultrasonic probe of elastic anisotropy in textured steel plates. Directional laser-ultrasonic measurements were performed on 70% cold-rolled Ti-stabilized interstitial-free steel plates in the full-hard and recrystallized condition. Experimental results were compared with predictions based on effective elastic stiffness tensors derived from X-ray diffraction measurements. Classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill estimates and microstructure-resolved finite-element homogenization reproduce the measured angular dependence of the ZGV frequencies well for both states, with the finite-element KUBC/SUBC bounds considerably narrower than the classical Voigt-Reuss bounds. For the full-hard state, agreement with the texture-based model is obtained only after a recovery treatment. This indicates that dislocations present in the full-hard material contribute to its elastic response, an interpretation that is further supported by theoretical estimations. An identifiability analysis shows that the directional ZGV measurements provide access to at least three independently observable combinations of the stiffness tensor components, and concluding suggestions for application in recrystallization monitoring are provided.

title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

title: Confirmation of complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ by broad range $^{139}$La-NQR
abstract: The transition metal oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ exhibits a non-collinear spin-ice like antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N \approx $ 90 K due to complex magnetic exchange interactions and axial single-ion anisotropy of Fe$^{2+}$ spins. The magnetic structure was deduced/determined from combined $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and $^{139}$La-NMR on polycrystalline specimen. In this work, we present zero-field $^{139}$La-NQR investigations on polycrystalline La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ in a broad frequency and temperature range between 2.8 - 20 MHz and 4.2 - 100 K. The measured resonances at $ν_Q$, $2 \, ν_Q$, and $3 \, ν_Q$ are fully consistent with the previous NMR studies and also with the magnetic structure. A substantial modification of the electric field gradient at the La-position below $T_N$ is inconsistent with the current investigations.

title: Perpendicular Magnetization from Crystallite Boundaries in Polycrystalline Antiferromagnetic $γ$-FeMn
abstract: Single-crystalline noncollinear antiferromagnets, such as Mn$_3$Sn, are actively explored as memory media, but they generally require high-temperature growth that is incompatible with industrial-scale device fabrication. Here, we show that polycrystalline films of antiferromagnetic $γ$-FeMn, grown at room temperature, develop a perpendicular magnetization and an anomalous Hall effect, opening an industrially compatible route to antiferromagnetic memory. While conventional noncollinear antiferromagnets demand near-perfect crystal order, $γ$-FeMn films derive their memory-enabling properties from crystal defects, particularly boundaries separating nanoscale crystallites. When the crystallite size $D$ falls below $\approx$ 30 nm, a field-switchable magnetization emerges and increases with the boundary density $\propto 1/D$. This magnetization is accompanied by a room-temperature anomalous Hall conductivity exceeding 10 S/cm, comparable to that of single-crystalline Mn$_3$Sn. Our systematic experimental results, including scanning magnetometry, indicate uncompensated spin moments in the boundaries coupled to the compensated antiferromagnetism within the crystallites. We further find that the perpendicular easy axis of the magnetization is stabilized by residual strain within the $γ$-FeMn film. Our findings in manufacturing-friendly polycrystalline $γ$-FeMn redefine crystal defects as enablers, rather than impediments, for scalable antiferromagnetic memory.

title: Mechanism of delayed elastic state absorption versus fatigue failure in cyclic shear of amorphous materials
abstract: We study cyclic shear in a lattice elastoplastic model of amorphous materials. The model displays a threshold shear amplitude $γ_{\rm c}$, which increases with sample annealing. For imposed amplitudes $γ_0\lesssimγ_{\rm c}$, it shows slow progression to an absorbing elastic state. For $γ_0\gtrsim γ_{\rm c}$, it shows slow fatigue and delayed material failure. Our key contribution is to elucidate a mechanistic understanding of this behaviour. We show that progression to an absorbing state maps to single element diffusion on a finite interval with two absorbing boundaries. We derive expressions for the decay rate of the fraction of active elements, and the survival distribution. The diffusing variable is the local elemental strain, which takes two jumps stroboscopically per cycle. Once the value at any site diffuses below its yielding threshold, the element behaves elastically. This leads to a gradual accumulation of strains just below threshold. For $γ_0\lesssim γ_{\rm c}$ this diffusive behaviour is preceded by many cycles in which cooperativity between elements via stress propagation is also important. For $γ_0 > γ_{\rm c}$, stress propagation dominates and precipitates failure. For $γ_0\gtrsim γ_{\rm c}$, the same accumulation of elements just below local threshold that led to an elastic state for $γ_0\lesssimγ_{\rm c}$ accounts for the fatigue that brings the system to the brink of failure. We evidence this via simulations in which the strain amplitude artificially exceeds $γ_0 $ in each half cycle, before reverting to the system's actual state at $\pmγ_0$ and resuming the next half cycle. During fatigue, the stress-strain slope $dσ/dγ$ evolves towards unity at $|γ|=γ_0^-$, signifying perfect elasticity within cycle, yet towards zero at $|γ|=γ_0^+$, precipitating failure.

title: Machine Learning-Based Taylor Cone Analysis for Electrospinning Process-Window Identification and Cell-Laden Nanofiber Scaffold Fabrication
abstract: Electrospinning is a powerful biofabrication technique for constructing fibrous scaffolds that mimic extracellular matrix architectures. However, the process is highly nonlinear and involves strongly coupled parameters, making fiber architecture and biological performance difficult to control empirically and limits reproducibility. Most machine learning (ML) studies still focus on static correlations between processing parameters and outcomes rather than on dynamic modeling of electrospinning evolution and regulation, thereby hindering real-time, precise process control.

title: Information-theoretic approach to density-based machine learning
abstract: Density-based machine learning encompasses several distinct tasks: predicting an electron density or Hamiltonian, learning Kohn-Sham (KS) exchange-correlation or orbital-free kinetic-energy functionals, and using a computed density to predict a higher-level molecular property. This Perspective focuses on the last route and asks when quantities from the information-theoretic approach (ITA) provide a useful, physically interpretable compression of the electron density.

title: Cellulose Coating Altered the Electro-Chemo-Mechanical Evolution of Sodium Thioantimonate Electrolyte in Solid-state Sodium Batteries: An Operando Raman Study
abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) attracted increasing attention due to their improved safety and energy densities; yet electrolyte decomposition and subsequent contact loss limited the interfacial stability of ASSBs. Herein, we report an operando Raman characterization that provides high voltage, time, and spatial resolutions, which enables simultaneous analysis of interfacial decomposition mechanism and morphological evolution.

title: Poly(Ionic Liquid)-Engineered Interfacial Water Reorganization for Selective Acidic CO2-to-Formic Acid Electroreduction
abstract: Acidic CO2 electroreduction offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization compared with alkaline or neutral systems. However, maintaining high product selectivity at industrially relevant current densities remains challenging because local CO2 depletion and excessive proton availability intensify the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we develop a bismuth sulfide (Bi2S3) catalyst modified with a long-chain imidazolium poly(ionic liquid) layer (PIL@BS) for electrocatalytic CO2-to-formic acid conversion at pH 2.

title: Super-tetragonal ferroelectric barium titanate through anionic overstoichiometry
abstract: Ferroelectric oxides, characterized by an electrical polarization that is switchable with an electric field, are an appealing class of materials for energy-efficient computing, electronics, and photonics. In thin films, the properties of ferroelectrics are commonly tuned using substrate-imposed epitaxial strain, an approach limited to biaxial strain states and a finite number of available substrates. Here, we demonstrate that is is possible to move beyond conventional epitaxial growth by using pulsed laser deposition under highly non-equilibrium conditions. Specifically, we show that this unconventional processing route allows us to stabilize a super-tetragonal phase of ferroelectric $\text{BaTiO}_3$. The key to this stabilization lies in the insertion of surplus oxygen atoms into the unit cell, resulting in peroxide bond formation that give rise to an aspect ratio of as high as 1.08. Notably, this super-tetragonal phase exhibits an enhanced ferroelectric polarization, reduced coercivity, lower leakage currents, and increased cycling endurance compared to conventional bulk-like $\text{BaTiO}_3$ films. These results, thus, showcase the potential of non-equilibrium growth for defect engineering to obtain emergent phases in complex oxides and tune their physical properties in thin films expanding the scope of traditional epitaxy.

title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
abstract: Controlling transition rates is a central objective across quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical physics, encompassing processes such as spontaneous emission, energy and charge transfer, spin relaxation, and chemical reactions. Although Fermi's golden rule provides a powerful framework for calculating such rates of weakly coupled transitions, conventional calculations require the interaction to be specified in advance; the range of rate responses attainable over a broader interaction space remains unknown. We formulate spectral-overlap golden-rule rates as quadratic forms of the interaction and derive rigorous bounds on rate modulation over a specified interaction space. As an example, application to energy transfer from a donor to a molecular vibration coupled to an optical cavity reveals that enhancement and suppression depend jointly on the interaction and cavity detuning, including continuous reversal of the rate response for a fixed interaction. The same approach may elucidate rate control for other golden-rule processes, including excitation-energy transfer, nonadiabatic electron transfer, nonradiative electronic transitions, vibrational and spin relaxation, and spontaneous emission.

title: Two-dimensional structures formed by pair potentials: An analytical and numerical study
abstract: Understanding the thickness dependence of the excess energy of thin films and identifying the deviation from the scaling law that holds for thicker films are crucial for predicting the formation of two-dimensional (2D) materials derived from nonlayered structures, commonly referred to as non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials. Here, we analytically study the excess energy of thin films as a function of the number of layers $N$, assuming pair potentials. We show that the $1/N$ scaling law of the excess energy breaks down in the monolayer limit when the interatomic interactions are long-ranged. The analytical results are confirmed by numerical simulations using the Lennard-Jones and Morse potentials. The present work suggests that non-vdW 2D structures can be formed by pair potentials alone.

title: Microscopic origin of field-induced multiferroicity in Ni3TeO6
abstract: The continued demand for smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient technologies has driven condensed-matter research towards materials combining multiple responses within a single phase. Particularly interesting examples are multiferroic materials featuring cross-couplings between order parameters. Ni3TeO6 is a prominent member of this material class, exhibiting a hysteresis-free transition under magnetic field which simultaneously affects the magnetic structure, electric polarization, and phonon frequencies. Here, we uncover the microscopic origin of this multiferroic transition using a combination of neutron scattering techniques. We establish the presence of a finite Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange term giving rise to non-reciprocal, chiral spin waves which soften in magnetic field. Their condensation alters the magnetic structure which controls the electric polarization and drives an ionic displacement, thereby coupling the magnetic, electric, and lattice degrees of freedom. Our study demonstrates that neutron scattering is a powerful technique to elucidate microscopic interactions in multiferroic materials, informing the design of next-generation electronic devices.

title: Photon Correlations Control Quantum Fisher Information in Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
abstract: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy probes interactions and dynamics of molecular systems through nonlinear optical signals. Quantum light excitation has been explored as a means of controlling these signals, raising the question of how excitation-light correlations affect the precision of molecular parameter estimation from the emitted signal. In this work, we show that photon-number correlations and two-photon coherence play distinct roles in encoding molecular information in the emitted rephasing signal. In the weak-emission regime and within the single Schmidt pair approximation, we derive a normally ordered information law in which the joint photon-number moment and the squared magnitude of the two-photon coherence weight the amplitude and phase sensitivities of the molecular response, respectively. For matched temporal modes and mean photon numbers in each input mode, two-mode squeezed vacuum enhances both weights relative to coherent excitation, whereas independent displaced squeezing preserves the amplitude weight but reduces the phase weight. The background population and its parameter dependence also affect the total quantum Fisher information, which therefore cannot be inferred from the coherent mean-field signal alone. We derive a leading-order bound on its enhancement over coherent excitation when the background population is nonnegative and common to the compared sources. These findings provide criteria for selecting excitation sources according to how the target molecular parameter affects the amplitude and phase of the response.

title: Spin-Adapted Spin-Flip Tamm-Dancoff Approximation (XSF-TDA) for Singlet-Triplet Gaps in MR-TADF and INVEST Emitters
abstract: In this work, we assess the recently introduced spin-adapted TDA for spin-flip-down excitations (XSF-TDA) [Mol. Phys. e2631735 (2026)] as a practical approach to this problem. Starting from a high-spin restricted open-shell Kohn--Sham reference, XSF-TDA generates spin-adapted low-spin roots arising from open--open (OO), core--open (CO), open--virtual (OV), and core--virtual (CV) types of spin-flip-down excitations. Across four application sets comprising 243 benchmark cases, XSF-TDA substantially reduces the systematic positive bias observed for TDA and unrestricted spin-flip TDA (USF-TDA). With the B3LYP functional, XSF-TDA reduces the equal-set-weighted macro-MAE relative to USF-TDA from 0.252 eV (0.158 eV) to 0.102~eV (0.056~eV) with the ALDA0 (multicollinear) kernel. Its accuracy is competitive with state-specific $Δ$DFT and quasiparticle-energy DFT (QE-DFT), while being able to provide deeper mechanistic insight through the response vector. In particular, spin-adapted CV configurations provide selected higher-excitation character that strengthens the OO--CV dynamical-spin-polarization channel, which preferentially stabilizes the singlet states. We also identify an INVEST emitter with appreciable OO--OV mixing, suggesting a possible additional contribution to singlet stabilization when the CV contribution is small. The XSF-TDA method therefore provides practical singlet--triplet gap predictions together with interpretable state analysis for the screening and mechanistic understanding of MR-TADF and INVEST emitters.

title: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4
abstract: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. The resulting AMR ratio reaches -33% at 8 K and 10 T and exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature dependence qualitatively captured by a minimal spin-disorder model. These results show that engineering the local environment of dilute magnetic ions provides a route to large paramagnetic AMR without long-range magnetic order, extending the materials design space for AMR beyond magnetically ordered systems.
