title: An Exact 93-Move Solution to a Nonlocal Crystal-Exchange Puzzle
abstract: We determine the minimum number of directional commands needed to solve alevel of Order of the Sinking Star, modeled as a crystal-exchangepuzzle on an 11*11 board. A command swapsthe player with the nearest crystal in the selected row or column, regardlessof distance; only an empty ray permits an ordinary unit walk. Two gates admitthe player to the exit exactly while all sixteen crystals occupy their targetcells. We give an explicit 93-command solution and exclude every shortersolution by an exact, cost-bounded breadth-first search. The search representsa position by its seventeen occupied cells and one active cell. Its admissibleheuristic partitions command costs between a compressed core abstraction andresidual motion, strengthened by a necessary activation detour and a cornervisit condition. The completed computation retained 605,349,215 occupied setsand 1,863,925,136 states. We prove the reductions and pruning conditions,describe the exact storage scheme, and provide source code, execution logs,and a reproduction driver. The result is a computer-assisted proof for thespecified instance, with an explicit implementation trust boundary.

title: Biochemistry professor says a scientist’s place is in the senate
abstract: Vying for a seat in the Indiana State Senate, David Sanders says we need more people with scientific expertise in elected office

title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion
abstract: X-ray and neutron scattering are indispensable for structural characterization across condensed-matter physics and materials science. Yet, because scattering experiments generally record intensities without phase information, distinct structures can yield similar scattering patterns, rendering the corresponding inverse problems non-unique. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining complementary measurements, but their integration into machine-learning frameworks remains challenging. Here we introduce a modular framework for probabilistic multi-measurement analysis based on prior-amortized flow matching. Single-observation posterior estimators are trained separately for individual observation types or physical probes and combined only at inference time through a compositional sampler. This late fusion approach allows pretrained single-observation models to be reused without dedicated joint retraining. As a case in point, we consider reflectometry, which provides depth-resolved, nanometer-scale information about thin films and interfaces. Our single-observation demonstrations span X-ray, time-of-flight neutron and polarized neutron reflectometry. In separate co-refinement studies, task-matched estimators enable homogeneous composition across multiple neutron contrasts and heterogeneous multimodal composition of X-ray and neutron measurements. Together, these results establish compositional flow matching as a modular approach to uncertainty-aware inversion and co-refinement, with potential applicability to other scattering problems in which multiple observations constrain a common physical structure while retaining measurement-specific parameters.

title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
abstract: The atomic ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys strongly influences their magnetic properties and mechanical behavior. While general features of long-range atomic ordering are known from the experimentally established phase diagram in this composition range, detailed atomic configurations and driving forces behind them remain speculative. Here, we address this gap by using effective cluster interactions (ECI) obtained from density functional theory (DFT) calculations and subsequent statistical thermodynamics modeling to unravel the interplay between magnetism, composition, and temperature in body-centered cubic (bcc) Fe-Si alloys up to 20 at% Si. Our analysis reveals that the ordering behavior is governed by a strong coupling between magnetic order, lattice expansion, and Si concentration, with specific ECI shells switching sign or magnitude as the magnetic state changes, which is reflected in the phase equilibria and ordering behavior of Fe-Si alloys. In particular, we demonstrate that D0$_3$ ordering is, in fact, primary in the totally ordered ferromagnetic state, while the B2 type of ordering is promoted in the paramagnetic state at elevated temperatures. The temperature-dependent evolution of these ordering patterns, obtained from Monte Carlo simulations based on the magnetically resolved ECIs, reproduces the experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range order characteristics. By explicitly linking the magnetic state with the effective interactions and macroscopic phase behavior, this work establishes a predictive framework for an ab initio-based description of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys and highlights the decisive role of magnetism in ordering phenomena in this system.

title: Tuning Thermal Memory and Dissipation in Colloidal Glasses via Microgel Particle Stiffness
abstract: The Kovacs effect, characterized by nonlinear, path-dependent structural recovery, is a hallmark of glassy systems. In soft colloidal microgel glasses, the stiffness of the constituent particles governs their deformation, swelling, rearrangement, and response to external stimuli, thereby dictating the path-dependent structural recovery of these jammed non-equilibrium systems. To investigate this influence, microgels of different stiffnesses were synthesized by adjusting the concentration of the polar crosslinker, N, N'-methylenebisacrylamide (MBA). The relaxation of the storage and loss moduli was measured using oscillatory rheology under diverse temperature ramp rates, and cryo-FESEM imaging provided direct visualization of the underlying particle packing. While the rapid adaptability of soft particles and the kinetic arrest of stiff ones suppresses Kovacs asymmetry, intermediate-stiffness particles exhibit moderate thermoresponsivity, traversing distinct energy landscapes on heating and cooling to maximize asymmetry and dissipation. Cryo-FESEM micrographs, displaying gel-like networks in soft particle suspensions, dense packing in stiff particle suspensions, and disordered, compact structures in intermediate-stiffness systems, corroborate these findings. Our results demonstrate that intermediate-stiffness PNIPAM microgels optimize structural recovery, rendering them promising candidates for forming colloidal glasses and establishing Kovacs asymmetry as a robust probe of non-equilibrium dynamics in glassy systems.

title: Synthetic W/Cu Mimics of the Mo/Cu Active Site in Aerobic CODH: Nonclassical Isocyanide Coordination and the Role of the Bridging Sulfide
abstract: Aerobic carbon monoxide dehydrogenase (CODH) uses an unsupported Mo–S–Cu heterobimetallic active site to catalyze CO oxidation, but the mechanistic role of the bridging sulfide remains to be fully resolved. We report a series of W/Cu complexes designed to test whether steric shielding from a bidentate tBuxantphos ligand can suppress unwanted Cu···Sdithiolate and Cu···O═M interactions that plagued the reactivity of a previously reported NHC-ligated model system.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
abstract: Analogical reasoning is widely considered a fundamental component of human intelligence. Few benchmarks are designed to explicitly test far analogical reasoning - reasoning between domains that are superficially dissimilar yet share deep relational or structural similarities. In this work, we introduce an analogical reasoning benchmark called Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy (ARCANA). The tasks of ARCANA require performing far analogical mappings from real-world objects or physical phenomena to abstract grid-based transformations, different from the well-known ARC-AGI benchmark which primarily emphasized innate human priors. We validate ARCANA through a human study, demonstrating that humans solve these tasks reliably. In contrast, evaluations across a range of large language models show a distinct performance gap compared to humans, revealing systematic failure modes that remain challenging for current models. To address this gap, we propose ConceptSIR, a reasoning framework based on concept slippage, introspection, and reflection. Experiments demonstrate that ConceptSIR enables standard LLMs to solve several challenging ARCANA tasks that were unsolved by direct prompting in our evaluation. Overall, our results suggest that far analogical reasoning remains an open problem for contemporary LLMs. All the materials are available at sites.google.com/view/arcanacogtest. The complete codebase, including benchmark, and ConceptSIR, is publicly available at https://github.com/density-11/arcana-test. All ARCANA data and task instances can be accessed and explored at https://arcanacogtest.org/.

title: Higher-Order Flatband-Touching Points Mediate Unconventional Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
abstract: The bulk-boundary correspondence establishes a fundamental connection between bulk band topology and the emergence of boundary states, underpinning topological phenomena across electronic, acoustic, photonic, and many other wave systems. A broad class of singular flatband systems, however, exhibits an unconventional form of bulk-boundary correspondence, in which robust boundary modes (RBMs) originate from flatband-touching points (FBTPs) and the real-space topology associated with incomplete sets of compact localized states (CLSs), rather than conventional momentum-space bulk topological invariants. To date, experimental studies of such boundary modes have been limited to systems hosting lower-order FBTPs. Here, we experimentally demonstrate unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence in a photonic cross-bedded Kagome-like lattice featuring a higher-order FBTP formed by the touching of two degenerate flatbands and a dispersive band. Using continuous-wave laser writing, we observe shape-preserving propagation of both bulk CLSs and boundary RBMs. Remarkably, unlike previously reported flatband systems, the RBMs retain their boundary localization under input-field perturbations involving both singular and nonsingular CLSs, revealing an unconventional boundary response associated with the higher-order FBTP in this lattice. Our results establish the Kagome-like lattice as a new platform for exploring flatband physics and unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, with potential applications in wave localization, flatband lasers, and other emerging topological photonic devices.

title: Disorder-Mediated Magnetism in Transition-Metal Dichalcogenide Monolayers: XS$_2$ and XSe$_2$ (X = Ti, V, Co, Mo, and Ru)
abstract: Magnetism in transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers has attracted considerable attention, yet its nature remains elusive, particularly in monolayer 1T-VSe$_2$. Our first-principles calculations show that Stoner instability can drive ferromagnetism in XS$_2$ and XSe$_2$ monolayers (X = Ti, V, Co, Mo, and Ru), associated with a reduced density of states at the Fermi level. We demonstrate that mixing nonmagnetic Ti, Co, Mo, and Ru disulfides or diselenides can induce magnetism. Conversely, mixing magnetic VS$_2$ or VSe$_2$ with other compounds can completely suppress magnetism. Both scenarios can lower the total energy. Moreover, substituting a small number of V atoms with Co defects can also disrupt ferromagnetism in 1T-V(S,Se)$_2$. Even in pristine 1T-VSe$_2$, we find ferrimagnetic configurations with reversed local V moments that are nearly degenerate with the ferromagnetic state. Their competition may contribute to the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic order. This reduced energy penalty for magnetic and structural disorder arises from a suppressed density of states at the Fermi level, resembling the mechanism underlying the Peierls transition. Electronically driven energy lowering near the Fermi level may therefore be widespread among transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers in various forms.

title: From Scores to Safe Sets: Exact Safety--Constrained Decoding for Medication Recommendation
abstract: Recent generative medication recommendation systems ultimately produce sets of drugs, but drug--drug interaction (DDI) constraints depend on the set as a whole. A natural post-hoc approach is to first predict medications and then locally repair interacting pairs by removing one drug at a time. We ask whether this local repair step itself introduces avoidable error. Using fixed medication scores from FLAME's frozen classifier on MIMIC-III, we compare increasingly strong local repair strategies with an exact global decoder while holding the scores, output size, and DDI constraint fixed. The global decoder jointly selects the highest-scoring feasible medication set using mixed-integer linear programming. Across validation and test splits, global decoding consistently achieves higher Jaccard similarity than greedy repair, degree-aware repair, and degree-aware repair strengthened with exhaustive 1-swap local search. Its advantage is small under loose DDI constraints and becomes larger as the constraint tightens; on the test split it reaches +0.0064 Jaccard over the strongest local baseline at the strict DDI operating point. The finding also holds across a fine accuracy--DDI sweep at matched realized DDI exposure and under three score representations. At the strict setting, global decoding retains more true-positive medications while removing more false positives. These results show that medication recommendation is not only a representation-learning problem: even with a frozen clinical model, how its scores are converted into a constrained medication set can materially affect the final prediction.

title: Binder migration across film consolidation and pore emptying in electrode drying: a continuous model validated against drying-rate, thickness, and schedule experiments
abstract: Drying battery electrodes faster saves energy but drives dissolved binder toward the film surface, depleting the current-collector interface and weakening adhesion. Models of this migration stop convecting the binder when film consolidation ends, and models of the subsequent pore emptying omit the binder or start from an assumed binder field, so no simulation has followed binder convection through both stages that a drying schedule acts on. This study presents a continuous simulation of the dissolved binder field across both stages, driven by the published drying rates and completed by effective descriptions of the two questions the base transport physics leaves open: where the liquid of the consolidating film carries the binder, and when the binder stops moving as the pores empty. With a single parameter set, the simulation reproduces three types of published measurements: the change of the surface-to-interface binder ratio with drying rate over a factor of 5.6 and the surface and interface binder levels of films six times thicker; concentration profiles through the film interior; and the response of the interface binder to the time at which the drying rate is switched mid-process. Applied without further adjustment to a published three-stage schedule, the model reproduces the shortened drying and the full interface recovery when the rate is lowered early, and shows that its final high-rate stage begins after the binder has stopped. Combined with a coater-scale process model, the model can be used to identify operating points for electrode production that improve energy efficiency and product quality together.

title: Characterization of pharmacological inhibition of the hERG potassium channel by nitazene opioids
abstract: Nitazene opioids are ‘street’ drugs, many of which are substantially more potent than heroin. They are linked to respiratory depression, but other adverse effects have not been widely investigated. Machine learning models have predicted that several nitazenes may interact with a major drug anti-target, the hERG cardiac potassium channel. This study was conducted to evaluate effects on hERG of isotonitazene, protonitazene, etonitazene, metonitazene and the related piperadine benzimidazoline brorphine. hERG-expressing HEK293 cells were studied using automated patch clamp.

title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.

title: Coherent dynamics and ultrafast evolution of optical nonlinearity of self-hybridized exciton-polaritons in WSe2
abstract: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Here, we show pronounced coherent dynamics in thin flakes of WSe2 supporting self-hybridized EPs. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. Rapid evolution of 2DES line shape indicates a change of dominant optical nonlinearities from Rabi contraction of polaritons to many-body interactions of excitons in the first 100 fs, marking the transition from coherent to incoherent polariton excitations. The results are rationalized by a three-coupled oscillator model considering the inhomogeneous cavity field distribution. We also demonstrate coherent quantum beating between A exciton and its excited Rydberg state A* under ambient conditions. Our results shed light on the coherent control in readily accessible semiconductor thin flakes.

title: SU(2)-Equivariant Spinor Message Passing for Molecular Magnetism
abstract: Predicting molecular magnetism often requires electronic-structure calculations with spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which are costly to repeat across many molecules. The underlying electronic states can transform as spinors, yet equivariant surrogates typically use only integer-rank features. Inspired by the spinor nature of these electronic states, we develop eSpinor, an SU(2)-equivariant graph neural network that propagates spinor features. We initialize spinor features from eigenvectors of an approximate SOC Hamiltonian and use gauge-covariant message passing with a gauge-invariant readout to make predictions independent of the arbitrary eigenbasis choice. On cobalt single-molecule magnet candidates, eSpinor improves zero-field-splitting predictions relative to NequIP, including for unseen ligands. For a dysprosium magnetic resonance imaging probe, eSpinor improves real electron-spin correlations over a Hamiltonian-informed baseline despite similar static crystal-field errors and fewer parameters, while accurately predicting low-field nuclear relaxation in water and after transfer to methanol without retraining. Overall, these results demonstrate that SU(2)-equivariant spinor message passing is a useful inductive bias for molecular magnetism. We also find that similar static tensor errors can yield different dynamical errors, motivating model selection based on accuracy for the intended physical observables.

title: Geometry and electronic properties of chiral phosphorene nanotubes
abstract: Phosphorene nanotubes (PNTs) exhibit highly tunable electronic properties, yet research has largely focused on high-symmetry armchair and zigzag configurations. This work presents the first systematic study of the geometric and electronic properties of chiral PNTs. Using the Chiraltube software, a comprehensive set of 214 PNTs was generated and analyzed via a 2D zone-folding mapping approach. Subsequently, a representative subset of 48 chiral PNTs was selected for ab initio calculations covering the full chiral space. While the mapping method overestimates band gaps by directly inheriting monolayer features, it serves as a qualitative tool for specific chiral geometries-particularly armchair configurations and larger-radius tubes-by effectively capturing their subband density and dispersion profiles. Finally, this work details the evolution of structural stability and electronic properties as a function of radius and chirality, identifying clear direct-to-indirect band gap transitions driven by curvature effects, alongside metallic behavior in specific zigzag configurations.

title: Analytic Derivative Couplings for MRSF-TDDFT: Applications to Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics and Conical Intersections
abstract: We present an analytic formulation of derivative couplings for mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT). Cross terms between the two states' excitation amplitudes and the orbital-rotation derivative of their wave-function overlap enter the interstate Lagrangian. Together they define the source of a state-pair Z-vector equation with the reference orbital Hessian, yielding the analytic derivative coupling vector. The analytic vectors enable conical-intersection searches using both branching directions.

title: Flexible force field-based screening and machine learning predictions for CO2 sorption and diffusion in MOFs
abstract: Machine learning offers an efficient route for screening metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), but most existing models rely on rigid-framework simulations that neglect framework flexibility. In this work, DFT-derived flexible force fields were used to calculate CO2 sorption and self-diffusion for 5,418 MOFs, providing the training data for machine-learning models capable of rapidly predicting these properties. We investigated different ML algorithms, featurization methods, and the role of physical descriptors in predicting CO2 sorption and self-diffusion in MOFs.

title: CO on Small Metal Clusters: Site-Resolved Vibrational Shifts and DMRG and VQE Benchmarks of Electron Correlation
abstract: Strong electron correlation in transition-metal chemistry motivates both advanced classical solvers, such as the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG), and quantum algorithms, but a claim of quantum utility requires a converged classical baseline. This baseline is established for a concrete problem, the C–O stretching signature of CO on small Mn clusters (M = Cu, Ag, Au, Pd, Pt; n = 2–5).

title: Crystalline core micelles
abstract: A micelle is defined as a loosely bound aggregation of several tens to hundreds of surfactant molecules, forming a colloidal particle. Micelles possess well-defined core and shell regions, both of which exist in a liquid-like state. This liquid-like character allows micelles to be dynamic structures, with surfactant molecules continuously exchanging within the micelle and between the micelle and bulk solution. In contrast to this classical model, we report rod-like reverse micelles with a well-defined three-dimensional crystalline core.

title: A Nickel–Capped Calcium Hydride: Implications for Diene Hydrometallation
abstract: We report here the synthesis and comprehensive characterization of a molecular nickel complex featuring a σ–[Ca–H–Ni] interaction. Although numerous σ–[E–H–M] species have been characterized, analogous complexes featuring heavier alkaline–earth hydrides remain exceptionally rare owing to their highly ionic and reactive nature. Reaction of [Ni(t,t,t–cdt)] (t,t,t–cdt = t,t,t–cyclododeca–1,5,9–triene) with the calcium hydride, [{(DippBDI)Ca(THF)}(μ–H)]2 affords [{(DippBDI)Ca(THF)(μ–H){Ni(t,t,t–cdt)}], representing the first well–defined Ca–H–M complex (where M = transition metal) characterized…

title: Benchmarking Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory Plus One Double (TDDFT-1D) for Potential Energy Surfaces
abstract: Time-dependent density functional theory plus one double (TDDFT-1D) improves on conventional TDDFT by including one specially chosen doubly excited electronic configuration. In this study, we evaluate the ability of that method to describe the ground-and excited-state potential energy surfaces (PESs) of selected model compounds relevant to photochemistry. We find that its accuracy is highly dependent on the given test case.

title: A substrate-versatile operando electrochemical cell for X-ray absorption spectroscopy
abstract: Operando characterization techniques allow the understanding of electrochemical energy materials under operating conditions, which is essential to design high-performance electrocatalysts. Here, we present a novel operando electrochemical cell designed for X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), enabling the simultaneous acquisition of electrochemical data, real-time oxygen detection, and XAS spectra on X-ray opaque electrodes. The incident X-ray beam reaches the sample through the electrolyte rather than through the substrate in contrast to the majority of other cells.

title: Thermodynamics and Kinetics of Ga Surface Segregation in Cu–Ga Nanoparticles across Composition and Particle Size
abstract: Cu–Ga nanoparticles are promising catalysts for thermochemical and electrochemical CO2 conversion, with their catalytic behavior determined by their surface composition. Here, we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to determine how Ga distributes within Cu–Ga nanoparticles depending on composition, size, and temperature. DFT results show that Ga forms a homogeneous solid solution within the bulk Cu lattice, whereas Ga-rich terminations are favored for surfaces.

title: Atomistic Origin of Transition-Metal Dissolution in Ni-Rich Cathodes: The Role of Oxygen Loss
abstract: High-voltage operation of Ni-rich cathodes accelerates degradation through surface reconstruction and transition-metal dissolution. Although these processes occur concurrently, their mechanistic relationship remains unresolved. Here, we identify oxygen loss as the unifying mechanism coupling cathode surface reconstruction and transition-metal release in LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2||graphite cells, consistent with the increased Ni deposition observed at the graphite anode.

title: Synthesis of Clickable Pyrazolo-fused N -heterocycles using a Diversity Oriented Clicking Strategy
abstract: Diversity-Oriented Clicking (DOC) provides a powerful platform for the rapid assembly of structurally complex, SuFEx-enabled molecules. Here, we report a regioselective, catalyst-free [3+2] cycloaddition between 2-substituted-alkynyl-1-sulfonyl fluorides (SASFs) connectors and N -iminium ylides to access a library of sulfonyl fluoride functionalized fused N-heterocycles. Under mild conditions, N -iminopyridinium ylides react smoothly with a range of aromatic and aliphatic SASFs to furnish pyrazolo[1,5- a ]pyridinyl sulfonyl fluorides as single regioisomers.

title: Defect Chemistry and Electronic Structure of α-Pu2O3: A Hybrid DFT Study of Charged Vacancies, Interstitials, and Antisites
abstract: Using state-of-the-art hybrid density functional theory, we systematically investigate the formation energetics and electronic structure of native charged point defects in α-Pu2O3, including plutonium and oxygen vacancies, interstitials, and antisite defects. We find that these defects induce significant local structural distortions and modify the magnetic properties of neighboring Pu ions. Furthermore, they lead to a redistribution of electronic states near the band edges and induce in-gap states, resulting in notable variations of the band gap.

title: Chiral Octahedral Metallomesogens with Δ/Λ Core Chirality: Extending Wallach's Rule from Crystals to Liquid Crystals
abstract: Chirality often induces marked structural changes in liquid crystals (LCs) and can even induce new phases. Where chirality resides in a mesogen is thus a fundamental question, but because mesogens favor planar structures, the effect of chirality at the molecular center (core chirality) on their assemblies has remained poorly understood. This Account explores this question with the octahedral tris(β-diketonato) family M-Cn (M = Ru, Ir), whose Δ/Λ configuration proves to be a decisive design element.

title: Distribution Function Analysis of Crystalline and Low-Dimensional Materials
abstract: Atomic pair distribution function (PDF) analysis from X-ray total scattering is a powerful methodology for determining atomic structure and arrangements across crystalline, disordered, nanostructured, and low-dimensional materials on both laboratory and synchrotron instruments. Fundamentally, PDF analysis relies on two core pillars—PDF data reduction from one-dimensional (1D) total scattering profiles and real-space structural modeling—often accompanied in rapid-acquisition experiments by upstream two-dimensional (2D) detector image processing.

title: Unveiling the Molecular Basis of Silver(I) Sequestration by Glutathione: Stoichiometry, Stability and Structure at Neutral pH
abstract: The complexation of Ag(I) ions by reduced glutathione (GSH) at neutral pH was studied by UV-vis, CD and NMR spectroscopies and mass spectrometry, aided by DFT calculations. A tetrameric Ag 4 (GSH) 4 complex was found to be the sole species at these conditions, containing the octagonal Ag 4 S 4 ring with digonal S-Ag-S coordination mode. The pH-independent stability constant of this complex was determined by competitive titrations with excess of thiosulfate ions as KAg4(GSH)4 = 1.6 × 10 67 M -7 .

title: CuPd Dilute Alloys Enhance Stability During CO2 Electroreduction in Zero-Gap Electrolyzers
Cryo-EM structure of the sub-50 kD PDZ-RhoGEF catalytic core-RhoA complex reveals an allosteric mechanism for GEF switch
abstract: PDZ-RhoGEF (PRG) drives cellular processes including migration through activation of the GTPase RhoA. The GEF switch (GS) is an accessory region N-terminal to the PRG catalytic core that significantly enhances its activity against RhoA, but its mechanism is unknown. We take an integrative structural biology approach, including cryogenic electron microscopy, to deduce the GS mechanism. Enzymatic assays define interactions between the GS and PRG catalytic core that are required for enhancement of activity. While SEC-SAXS data suggest that the GS does not alter the global structure of the catalytic core-RhoA complex, HDX-MS data reveal that the GS induces widespread stabilization, particularly in the RhoA switch regions. We determined a sub-4 angstrom resolution structure of 46 kD of the complex between the catalytic core and RhoA, revealing that Switch I is more flexible without the GS. Collectively, these data suggest both direct and allosteric factors in the mechanism of the GS.

title: A Microporous Zr-Tetraphosphonate MOF with Permanent Porosity, Robustness, and Thermochemical Heat Storage Capability
abstract: Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Vibrational Excitation of Water Drives Proton Reactivity with Native Proteins During Mid-Infrared Laser Desorption Coupled to Mass Spectrometry.
abstract: We discovered a vibrational-excitation-driven proton reactivity between proteins and their surrounding aqueous environment during mid-infrared laser Desorption by Impulsive Vibrational Excitation (DIVE). We show that this process, when coupled directly to high resolution mass spectrometry (MS) without secondary ionization sources, produces intact gas-phase ions of proteins retaining their compact conformations. The unexpected multiple protonation states of protein ions are generated through a series of concerted proton transfer processes to protein surface residues.

title: AMP Atlas: A Browser-Only Workbench for Antimicrobial Peptide Exploration and Interactive Helical-Wheel Design
abstract: Accessible research software can connect published antimicrobial peptide (AMP) records to sequence analysis, molecular visualization, and interactive design without requiring a dedicated application server. We present AMP Atlas, an open-source, browser-only workbench that combines a DRAMP-derived database with local physicochemical calculations, published-neighbor retrieval, and sequence-guided structural comparison. The reported snapshot contains 12,784 source records, 10,579 canonical records, 5,183 source SMILES annotations, and 433 PDB chain structures. An inverse helical-wheel editor lets users specify peptide length, fill residues gradually, and immediately retrieve exact-length database matches under positional and property constraints. Selected-position residue frequencies support further editing while preserving the remaining constraints. A Web Worker performs searches and numerical calculations; a WebGL viewer provides interactive molecular representations. The static distribution occupies 138.8 MB and supports GitHub Pages hosting. Verification includes 23 Python tests, 30 browser-core/worker checks, a designer DOM integration suite, and agreement against fixed numerical references. This report describes the implemented algorithms and assumptions; it does not establish predictive accuracy for antimicrobial activity or experimentally validate designed peptides. The website is available at https://hysonlab.github.io/amp-atlas/ and the source code and database are available at https://github.com/HySonLab/amp-atlas

title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature dependences, magnetic fields, and time-resolved measurements to establish microscopic assignments. The role of alloying as an additional degree of freedom for engineering the excitonic hierarchy, spin-valley configuration, and magneto-optical response is also highlighted. By organizing the rapidly expanding phenomenology around experimentally accessible fingerprints rather than individual material systems, this Review aims to provide a practical and broadly applicable guide for identifying, comparing, and engineering excitonic states in high-quality two-dimensional semiconductors.

title: QUBO-Based Conformer Selection with Quantum-Classical Hybrid Optimization for Multiconformer Ligand Modeling
abstract: A ligand can adopt multiple conformations within the same binding site, and these conformations can interact differently with the surrounding protein. Multiconformer modeling must therefore determine which candidate conformations to retain and what occupancies to assign to them. An established automated approach uses mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) with hard occupancy and conformer-count limits for this selection. Here, we reformulated conformer selection as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem with finite penalties and discrete occupancies. We solved the QUBO using a quantum-classical hybrid solver. We compared this workflow with the MIQP-based qFit-ligand workflow across 83 paired X-ray ligand entries using the same experimental inputs and the same qFit-ligand processing protocol. For each entry, both final models were evaluated against the same composite-omit map generated from the common input structure before the two workflows diverged. Quantum-qFit produced higher ligand-region real-space correlation coefficients (RSCC) in 62 entries 74.7% and lower occupancy-weighted torsional strain in 66 entries 79.5%. Similar directional trends remained in the 28 entries with matched final conformer counts. The molecular Electron Density for Individual Atoms score (EDIAm) decreased in most entries. This result shows that higher regional map agreement did not necessarily correspond to stronger atom-level density support. Overall, the results show that the conformer-selection formulation can change which ligand states are represented from the same experimental data and provide a QUBO framework for studying multiconformer ligand selection.

title: G-Quadruplex-Interacting Photooxidative Platinum(IV) Prodrug for Inhibiting Oncogene Transcription and Amplifying Antitumor Immunity
abstract: Conventional platinum (Pt)-based chemotherapeutics elicit cancer cell death primarily through DNA binding, but this approach is inherently limited by poor site specificity and a lack of spatiotemporal control, which compromises therapeutic precision and safety. To overcome these limitations, we report DNATplatin, an in situ activatable and photooxidative Pt(IV) prodrug designed to combine precise recognition of DNA secondary structures with targeted genetic intervention through DNA photooxidation. By incorporating a bis-N-methylpyridinium moiety to selectively recognize DNA, DNATplatin shows a 10-fold increase in the levels in genomic DNA relative to oxaliplatin and a 2.5-fold emission turn-on selectivity for G-quadruplexes (G4s) over typical duplex DNA. Following precise nuclear localization, photoactivated DNATplatin acts as a potent photooxidant that oxidizes G4, dismantles G4 scaffolds, and abrogates circular dichroism signatures. These orchestrated lesions generate localized oxidative stress and selectively silence major G4-driven oncogenes, thereby effectively circumventing traditional Pt resistance by bypassing canonical adduct-dependent pathways. In a murine triple-negative breast tumor model, DNATplatin produces profound tumor suppression and elicits a robust systemic immune response, characterized by CD4+/CD8+ T-cell activation and depletion of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. Collectively, this work establishes a controllable “target-and-destroy” strategy and underscores the potential of Pt(IV) photooxidants for topology-selective genetic intervention.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Copper-Mediated Valence Tautomerism Enables α -C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds and Tryptophans via Photocatalysis
abstract: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls.

title: Mapping Collective Electron-Density Rearrangements at Oil–Water Interfaces Using Optimal Transport
abstract: The electronic and spectroscopic properties of aqueous hydrophobic interfaces continue to be a topic of active research. One such open question is rooted in the origin of the apparent negative charge of oil droplets. Here, we deploy an information-theoretic optimal transport approach dubbed VIPER-CT (Voronoi-Informed Partitioning of Electron Redistribution for Charge Transfer), to construct the electronic T-matrix derived from the real-space electron density determined from first-principles simulations of an extended decane-water interface, sampled using neural-network-based Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics. This matrix operationally separates directional interphase charge transfer (CT) from intraphase density rearrangements. While decane-water molecular clusters of various sizes show small net CT from decane to water, the extended interface displays a systematic opposite electronic asymmetry, yielding a net CT from water to the hydrocarbon phase producing an average surface charge density of ∼0.003 e– nm–2 on the oil phase. This imbalance is accompanied by much larger intraphase self-polarization, particularly within the hydrocarbon phase, demonstrating that collective many-body polarization dominates the interfacial electronic response.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Functional architecture of rare protein coding variation across 786,871 exomes
abstract: Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits. Their functional effects can be predicted and categorized, particularly using machine learning models, and integrating these predictors benefits gene discovery. However, it remains unclear how well known structural features and predicted functional scores explain the heterogeneous effects of protein coding variants on human complex traits. We introduce the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), which integrates multiple functional annotations to form a kernel describing how allelic effects within a gene covary. We apply it to exome data from 26 traits and 786,871 individuals from UK Biobank and All of Us, integrating 35 annotations describing protein structure and predicting allelic effects. We estimate that rare missense heritability is at least 1.27±0.09% on average, 1.83±0.11% under our most flexible model, exceeding pLoF heritability (0.87±0.05%) and far exceeding missense burden heritability as previously estimated (0.54±0.04%). AlphaMissense is the single most enriched missense predictor, but a composite score doubles its enrichment. A series of structural features is enriched for heritability, from amino acid chemical features and structural motifs to residue contacts and protein-protein interaction interfaces. Examining pairs of variants, we find that most missense effects are modestly correlated, but an exception is when residues are close in 3D structure but distant in 1D sequence; such pairs also covary across species. Finally, we analyze individual genes and identify gene-specific enrichments, like a 95-fold enrichment among PIEZO1 hydrogen bond residues, that nominate functional hypotheses.

title: Energy Deposition Timescale Controls Chemistry in Pulsed Methane Plasmas
abstract: Nonoxidative methane conversion offers a promising route for the coproduction of hydrogen and value-added hydrocarbons without CO2 emissions. Among emerging approaches, pulsed plasmas can provide potential advantages by enabling high energy deposition, rapid quenching, and generation of active nonthermal species. This work systematically investigates how pulsed energy deposition from nanosecond-to-millisecond time scales (10 to 50 mJ/pulse) influences methane plasma characteristics (electron density and gas temperature), reaction mechanisms, conversion, and energy efficiency.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Pseudo-Icosahedral RhH2Au10 Superatom: Two Hydrogen Atoms Acting as Gold-Atom Equivalents and Modifiers
abstract: A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Leveraging genomic deep learning models for the prediction of noncoding variant effects
abstract: Characterizing noncoding variant function remains an important challenge in human genetics. Genomic deep learning models have emerged as a promising approach to enable in silico prediction of variant effects. These models include supervised sequence-to-activity models, which predict molecular phenotypes such as genome-wide chromatin states or gene expression levels directly from DNA sequence, and self-supervised genomic language models. Here we review progress in leveraging these models for noncoding variant effect prediction.

title: Computational Prediction of the Therapeutic Mechanisms From the Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix Seed Botanical Formula in Rheumatoid Arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by progressive synovial inflammation and immune-metabolic reprogramming. The polyphenol-rich Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix seed (TPC) formula shows therapeutic potential against RA, though its multi-target mechanisms remain uncharacterized. To explore how TPC modulates ferroptosis and oxidative stress in RA, we integrated systems nutrition network analysis with multicohort transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate targets. Ensemble machine learning algorithms and independent cohort validation prioritized key biomarkers. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations evaluated the dynamic behavior and interaction persistence of polyphenol-target complexes, and single-cell in silico overexpression and knockout analyses characterized the regulatory consequences of perturbing these targets within RA synovial networks. Analysis identified 85 bioactive phytochemicals in the TPC formula, forming a polyphenol-dominant matrix mapping to 40 RA targets. Algorithmic and cross-cohort prioritization isolated six core genes (ALOX5, CD38, CDK1, EZH2, MAPK8, and PTGS2) linked to RA synovial transcriptomic patterns, with varying predictive performance across external cohorts. SHAP analysis highlighted PTGS2, CD38, and MAPK8; however, MD simulations prioritized CD38 and MAPK8 as stable targets of coumestrol, whereas PTGS2 exhibited less dynamic stability. Single-cell perturbation analysis revealed similar regulatory responses following MAPK8 and PTGS2 modulation, whereas CD38 knockout produced a distinct network response. These findings link TPC-derived polyphenols to CD38/MAPK8 signaling and ferroptosis in RA, providing testable molecular hypotheses for experimental validation.

title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

title: Ultrasound-assisted proteolysis of pea protein: Structural and peptidomic modulation to enhance α-glucosidase inhibitory activity
abstract: With the increasing prevalence of diabetes mellitus, naturally derived α-glucosidase inhibitory peptides have garnered growing attention. Most studies have focused on preparation efficiency and bioactivity outcomes, while the structural mechanisms governing peptide release remain poorly understood. In this study, ultrasound-assisted proteolysis of pea protein was employed to elucidate how structural modifications regulate α-glucosidase inhibitory activity.

title: Code-driven planning in grid worlds with large language models
abstract: We propose an iterative programmatic planning (IPP) framework that solves grid-based tasks by using large language models (LLMs) to synthesize interpretable, executable programs that act as agent policies mapping environment states to action sequences, rather than relying on traditional search or reinforcement learning. Alongside prompting strategies such as direct code generation, pseudocode conditioned refinement and curriculum-based prompting, IPP centres on an iterative refinement mechanism that updates code from coarse, task-level feedback. We evaluate our approach using six leading LLMs and two challenging grid-based benchmarks (grid-based reasoning for assessing spatial planning (GRASP) and MiniGrid). Our IPP framework demonstrates improvements over direct code generation for five of the six models, with net energy gains ranging from a few per cent to roughly threefold and, for Gemini-2.5-Pro, a sign flip from a negative baseline to a strongly positive score, establishes a new state-of-the-art result for GRASP and significantly outperforms direct elicitation from GPT-o3-mini (by 43% on the hardest MiniGrid task to 116% on GRASP). While code generation has a higher initial prompting cost compared to direct solution elicitation ($0.08 per task versus $0.002 per instance for GPT-o3-mini), the code can be reused for any number of instances, making the amortized cost significantly lower (by 400 times on GPT-o3-mini across the complete GRASP benchmark). Beyond performance gains, IPP produces reusable, human-readable policies that support transparent inspection and modification, underscoring the advantages of planning as program synthesis over per-instance inference. The code and results can be found at http://github.com/Mystic-Slice/LLM-Planning-CodeGen.

title: Liposomal DAGLβ Inhibitor Shows Substantial Antinociceptive Potency Mediated by AMPK in a Neuropathic Pain Mouse Models
abstract: Diacylglycerol lipase-beta (DAGL{beta}), a biosynthetic enzyme for the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), is highly expressed in macrophages and serves as a potential contributor to inflammatory and hypernociceptive responses. Moreover, the DAGL{beta} inhibitor KT109 produces antinociceptive effects in various rodent pain models, and its liposome formulation dramatically increases its antinociceptive potency in a lipopolysaccharide mouse model of inflammatory pain compared to free KT109.

title: Computational fracture modelling of polymer-bonded explosives and solid propellants: A critical review of local and nonlocal continuum formulations and discrete particle approaches
abstract: Fracture behaviour is a critical determinant of the safety, reliability and service life of polymer-bonded explosives (PBXs) and solid propellants. Both are highly filled polymer composites whose damage evolution is governed by heterogeneous particle-binder architectures, rate- and temperature-dependent binders, interfacial debonding, matrix failure and particle or crystal fracture.

title: Discovery of a brain-penetrant CHI3L1 inhibitor as an oral modulator of neuroinflammation in Alzheimers disease
abstract: Chitinase-3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1) is elevated in Alzheimers disease (AD), but its role in glial dysfunction and therapeutic tractability remain unclear. Here, screening a 4.2-billion-compound DNA-encoded library identified DELC2, a brain-penetrant CHI3L1 modulator. Biophysical and crystallographic studies showed that DELC2 binds the CHI3L1 glycan-recognition groove within an aromatic-hydrophobic pocket centered on Trp99 and Trp352.
